note: Synthetic test material. The product and incidents are fictional.

nominal.input:
Generate our E2E test plan. Product: multi-tenant project-management SaaS (Next.js + Node API + PostgreSQL). Test stack: Playwright against a staging environment with Stripe in test mode. CI budget for E2E: 15 minutes per pull request, plus a nightly run with no limit.

Critical journeys:
1. Signup with email verification, then workspace creation
2. Invite a teammate; invited user accepts and gets the 'member' role
3. Upgrade to a paid plan via Stripe Checkout; access unlocks when the checkout.session.completed webhook arrives
4. Create, edit and delete a project; members cannot delete, admins can
5. Password reset
6. Export all projects as CSV (runs as a background job, emailed link)

Last quarter's incidents: a duplicated Stripe webhook upgraded a workspace twice and double-counted seats; a member of workspace A could open a project URL from workspace B.
expectedFindings: Includes the paid-upgrade journey with a duplicated or delayed webhook scenario that checks idempotent seat counting.
Includes a negative cross-tenant test where a user from one workspace requests another workspace's project URL and is denied.
Covers the asynchronous CSV export through completion and failure, rather than only the click that starts it.
Splits the suite between the 15-minute pull-request budget and the nightly run with an explicit rationale.
nominal.rationale: Past incidents give two concrete regressions the plan must encode, and the CI budget forces prioritization instead of exhaustive coverage.

regression.input: We migrated our E2E suite from Cypress to Playwright and moved CI from Node 20 to Node 24 at the same time. Since then the checkout test has failed 3 times in 40 runs, always with a timeout waiting for the 'Plan: Pro' badge. A teammate proposes deleting the checkout test because 'it is flaky' and accepting the migration because 36 of 40 runs were green. Update the test plan for this change.
expectedFindings: Refuses to delete or silently ignore the checkout test; treats the intermittent failure as a signal to investigate (for example webhook timing) with an owner, quarantine rule or deadline.
Requires recording the tool and runtime versions, browser versions and test-data or seed setup so results before and after the migration are comparable.
Requires re-running previously failing and high-risk journeys before accepting the migration, instead of relying on the overall green rate.
regression.rationale: Two simultaneous changes and a tempting pass rate test whether the plan protects a high-risk regression instead of averaging it away.
